newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: FISCHER SAYS THERE WILL BE WIDE CONSULTATION ON TCF TARIFFS
The Acting Prime Minister says the Government will consult widely before making a decision on tariff cuts in the Textile, Clothing and Footwear Industries.
Tim Fischer says the Productivity Commission's final report due out in September, will be carefully evaluated.
The Commission has recommended tariffs be reduced to five percent by 2008.
THOUSANDS OF JOBS FROM DEREGULATION: ALSTON
The Federal Communications Minister says he expects thousands of jobs to be created out of the de-regulation of the telecommunications market which starts at midnight tonight.
Richard Alston says new phone companies will need to employ people to install and run services.
Senator Alston is also confident new players will bring prices down, and is urging consumers to do their research.
He says cost of average international calls could fall by up to 60 percent, and already in Ballarat, residents are set to receive free local calls and reduced STD rates.
The Minister says there will also be financial penalties payable to consumers if they receive poor service from telecommunications companies.
LEGAL ACTION TO PREVENT RE-OPENING OF COPPER MINE DISMISSED
Legal action to prevent the re-opening of the Port Kembla copper smelter in 1999 has been formally dismissed in the Land and Environment Court today.

Port Kembla resident Helen Hamilton last month went to Court to try and halt the re-opening of the smelter by Japanese investors, but her legal action was overridden by the Government's special legislation supporting the redevelopment.
After the legislation recently passed through State Parliament's Upper House, the matter was today formally dismissed in the Land and Environment Court in Sydney.
Helen Hamilton warned that the smelter expansion will make the facility the state's largest polluter of lead and sulfur-dioxide but the Government maintained the development will mean jobs.
FINANCE MINISTER TO OVERSEE GOVT BUSINESS ENTERPRISES
Finance Minister, John Fahey will oversee the performance of all 14 Government Business Enterprises under new rules effective from today.
Under a joint arrangement the Finance Minister will share the responsiblity with the Minister responsible for the portfolio in which the enterprise falls.
Mr Fahey says the Ministerial shareholder arrangement will increase focus on the financial performance of government business enterprises.

The change is a key recommendation of a review of the relationship between the Commonwealth and its business enterprises, conducted by Managing Director of the Australian Stock Exchange, Richard Humphrey.
LETTERS SHED LIGHT ON TASMANIAN MURDER-SUICIDE
Police have shed some light on the reason for yesterday's family killing in Southern Tasmania.
Detective Inspector John Warren says police are still working to establish the real motive behind Peter Shoobridge killing himself and his four daughters at his property near Cambridge.
Inspector Warren says letters addressed to family members have given police a clue to yesterday's murder-suicide.
He says a couple of letters he has seen revealed some degree of frustration and disappointment by Mr Shoobridge about a number of issues.

"He certainly gave some indication that because of troubles if you like within the world today he didn't want to expose his children to those troubles. But apart from that I really can't go into it any further." Inspector Warren said.
However, he said it would be up to the Coroner, Ian Matterson, who has formally identified the victims to establish a motive for the deaths.
Meanwhile, three more letters from Peter Shoobridge have been recovered by police.
The letters were delivered in person by Mr Shoobridge to his closest neighbours.
BACTERIA SPREADING IN AUSTRALIAN HOSPITALS
A medical conference in Sydney has been told that a strain of bacteria, resistant to antibiotics, is spreading with ease in hospitals throughout Australia.
A dramatic rise in cases of the potentially-fatal bacteria has been described by an associate professor from Adelaide's Women's and Children's Hospital.
Associate Professor John Turnidge said the bacteria VRE had been identified in more than 30 clinical cases throughout Australia.
He described this as a dramatic increase since VRE had been first detected in Melbourne three years ago.
Professor Turnidge told the International Congress of Chemotherapy, the bacteria was seen most commonly in people with suppressed immune systems, such as transplant and chemotherapy patients.

He said it was difficult to know how many people had died from it, because those infected were usually very ill already. The congress was also told the anti-biotic resistant bacteria had ecome major problem in the United States, where it had started to spread from hospitals to nursing homes.
ACTU WATCHING EMPLOYERS OVER SUPER
The ACTU says it will take action against employers who cause their workers to lose money by switching their superannuation payments into new Retirement Savings Accounts.
The new lower interest paying Retirement Savings Accounts take effect tomorrow and can be opened as an alternative to superannuation funds.

ACTU President Jennie George has engaged Melbourne solicitors Slater and Gordon to take action against employers who cause financial loss to their workers by forcing them into opening Retirement Savings Accounts.

The ACTU believes it's generally accepted that while RSAs are a capital guaranteed product to be offered by banks and other financial institutions, they're expected to return lower crediting rates than superannuation funds.
HERBERT LOOKING FORWARD TO TAKING THE FIELD AGAINST ALL BLACKS

In rugby union, with Wallaby centre Jason Little unlikely to play in Saturday's test against New Zealand, replacement Danial Herbert says he's looking forward to his first match against the All Blacks.
Little suffered a torn muscle at the weekend and Herbert has been recalled in the only change to the squad.
Herbert says he is not concerned about coming into the side at short notice because he went to school with centre Pat Howard and played beside him for Queensland
He says while he has played against other New Zealand sides, he's been on the bench twice against the All Blacks, and is expecting the toughest game of his life.
